requirement_text.REQ-054: Port src/engine/snapshot_writer.zig (348 lines -- R-Co's ISS-601, design artefact src/design/iss601_state_snapshots.md) as Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter, plus its instance_state_snapshots migration and Ecto.Schema module (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, same as every other table this stage adds). THIS REQUIREMENT EXTENDS REQ-053's already-shipped reconstruct path -- it is not a standalone module. REQ-053 builds full-log replay from sequence 1; this requirement adds the snapshot table, the writer, and the replay-source selection that lets that same reconstruct function start from the latest snapshot instead. The deliverable is therefore a modification of REQ-053's function plus new supporting code, and the correctness bar below is that both paths agree. Purpose: reconstruction (REQ-053) replaying the FULL event log from sequence 1 is O(events) and gets slower forever. A periodic snapshot of the InstanceState as a jsonb blob lets reconstruction replay only the events SINCE the latest snapshot. - take_snapshot/N: serialises REQ-044's InstanceState (status, tokens, variables, pending task nodes, error_detail) plus the sequence_number it is current as of, into an instance_state_snapshots row. - maybe_take_snapshot/N: the cadence check -- snapshot every N events, default 1000 per snapshot_writer.zig's DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL. Called after event appends and on instance completion. - REQ-053's replay-source selection: given a latest snapshot at sequence S, replay only events with sequence_number > S on top of the deserialised snapshot state, versus replaying from 1 when no snapshot exists (reconstruction.zig's determineReplaySourceForSnapshot()). This requirement extends REQ-053's reconstruct path to use snapshots when present -- and the correctness bar is that BOTH paths produce the identical state, since a snapshot that diverges from full replay is worse than no snapshot at all. - This table is NOT the same thing as REQ-027/REQ-033's instance_definition_snapshots (the immutable PD-08 DEFINITION graph bound to an instance at start). These are periodic EXECUTION STATE snapshots, mutable in the sense that new rows accumulate over an instance's life. Say so explicitly in the moduledoc -- the two names are one word apart and confusing them would be a silent data-model error. OPEN QUESTION (flag, do not silently resolve): where the events-since-last-snapshot counter lives. instance_projections.last_event_seq (REQ-023) already tracks the latest sequence per instance, which makes a pure row-based cadence check possible with no in-memory counter at all; R-Co's own SnapshotWriter is a struct holding a pool handle. If REQ-045 resolved to supervised processes, an in-process counter is available but is exactly the kind of state stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding warns is NOT automatically worth a process. Leave the choice to CODE-DESIGNER, citing that finding and REQ-045's resolution.

task.description: Re-check security gate on REQ-054 after rework iteration 1 (commit 3207741 on feature/WF02-REQ054-20260819). ELIXIR-DEV wired SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 into lib/letflow/engine.ex's create/2, complete_task/3 (both :completed and :execution_error outcomes), and set_instance_error/2. The last call site introduced a new Engine -> Reconstruction dependency (calling Reconstruction.reconstruct_instance/2 to obtain an InstanceState when none is naturally in scope) -- flagged by ELIXIR-DEV itself for review. git diff main...HEAD for the full scope; git show 3207741 for just this iteration's delta.

result.summary: Full re-check against git diff main...HEAD (not just commit 3207741's delta), same rigor as a first pass. Scope test: diff touches a tenant-scoped migration (instance_state_snapshots), a new tenant-scoped Ecto schema/module (SnapshotWriter, InstanceStateSnapshot), and modifies Reconstruction's replay-source selection -- INV-1 applies. No API route, no untrusted-runtime path, no lookup-by-ID endpoint added -- INV-2/3/5 remain NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started). Per-invariant verdicts: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) APPLIES, PASS -- (a) every Repo call in snapshot_writer.ex (take_snapshot/4's Repo.insert, latest_snapshot/2's Repo.one) and reconstruction.ex's widened read_full_log/3 passes prefix: prefix explicitly, no default-schema fallback; (b) the migration wraps table+both indexes in `if prefix() do`, matching every other tenant-scoped migration's guard pattern, and is registered as the 28th entry in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.@tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (verified in tenant_provisioning.ex diff); (c) no tenant_id column exists on instance_state_snapshots at all (Decision 0006 D2), consistent with every table added since D2, so (c) does not apply here as a separate check. Traced prefix provenance at all three new engine.ex call sites: create/2, complete_task/3, and set_instance_error/2 each resolve `prefix = Keyword.get(opts, :prefix)` once at the top of the public function, validate it via `TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix)` in the same `with` chain, and thread that single validated binding unchanged through to persist/8, run_complete_task/6, and the ExecutionError.append_multi/3 call respectively -- the value passed into snapshot_instance/4 (and into maybe_snapshot_after_set_instance_error/3's Reconstruction.reconstruct_instance/2 call) is never re-derived, defaulted, or taken from a second source, so no cross-tenant misdirection is possible at any of the three sites. instance_id at the set_instance_error/2 site is likewise the single cast_instance_id from that same attrs map, paired with the same validated prefix -- Reconstruction.reconstruct_instance/2 is scoped to exactly the instance/tenant pair set_instance_error/2 was called for, cannot cross tenant boundaries. Failure-swallowing pattern (Logger.warning + continue) checked at all three call sites: in each of maybe_snapshot_after_create/4, maybe_snapshot_after_complete_task/2, and maybe_snapshot_after_set_instance_error/3, the snapshot/reconstruction attempt runs strictly after `|> Repo.transaction()` has already committed the event-log write, and every clause (including the {:error,_} branches) returns `result` -- the pre-existing, already-committed transaction outcome -- unchanged; a SnapshotWriter or Reconstruction failure can only suppress a future snapshot, never the durable event-log write that already happened, so tenant isolation and durability of the source-of-truth log are unaffected by snapshot failure. Confirmed the case in maybe_snapshot_after_set_instance_error/3 is exhaustive against Reconstruction.reconstruct_instance/2's own @spec ({:ok, reconstruct_result()} | reconstruct_error()`, where last_sequence_number :: non_neg_integer() | nil is the only two-way split needed) -- no CaseClauseError is reachable (INV-8). INV-4 (secrets) APPLIES (repo-wide check, unaffected by this diff), PASS -- grep for System.get_env/hardcoded-secret patterns unaffected by this diff; Logger.warning calls in the new code log only instance_id/sequence_number/inspect(reason), no secret material. INV-7 (no raw SQL) APPLIES, PASS -- grep -rn Repo.query across the diff's files: zero hits; all queries in snapshot_writer.ex and reconstruction.ex go through Ecto.Query/import Ecto.Query composition. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) APPLIES, PASS -- verified above for all three new call sites plus the pre-existing pattern in the rest of the diff; no bare {:ok, x} = external-call match introduced. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE (no API surface, no untrusted-runtime path, no lookup-by-ID endpoint in this diff -- S4/S5 not started). INV-6 (meta-invariant) satisfied by this handoff itself. No BLOCKER found; the two-way Engine<->Reconstruction module coupling ELIXIR-DEV flagged is an architectural/idiom question, not a tenant-isolation or invariant violation -- routed to REVIEWER per the handoff's own instruction, not a SECURITY-REVIEWER concern.
